name: 1706 Prairie Avenue — George Glessner Georgian townhouse, south of the pair, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling), '3B brick dwelling'; carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2334) in place under this id by T-1871: a K01 frontage built by generators/k01_emit.py from the 1911 sheet's outline of the pair (trace s20fp-1700-b1; census s20-1706-f) and the two photographs of the townhouses' front, Chicagology's and the Glessner House Museum's Christmas print, through the cameras T-3188 solved on that front (data/reference_views/george_glessner_house_1706_prairie/). The pair is mirrored: each house's porch and rear range stand at its outer end.

documented_range.note: The 1911 sheet draws the pair and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); the Christmas print, after 1902, shows its front as built here. Its building and loss dates are the next piece's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1706 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1700 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear south corner of the front block: in 1708 Prairie's frame, where T-3188 read the 1911 trace s20fp-1700-b1, at u -0.33 (the trace's step behind the front block, 13.1 m behind the front at u 12.77) and v 7.5 (the pair's south corner against 1708). Through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.581 degrees is 1708's, the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is the 1904 trace read in 1708 Prairie's frame (data/structures/house_1708_prairie.json) at the corner the note names.

footprint.note: The front block: the trace's 13.1 m from its step to the front, and 11.05 m along the street from the pair's south corner to the party line (T-3188's reading of the trace: v 7.5, 18.55 and 29.75 in 1708's frame). The rear range is in rear_wings.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet over the pair (T-1840 census s20-1706-f): the two brick storeys over a basement under a mansard storey, which both photographs show; K01 counts the walled storeys and the mansard holds the third.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the pair pink (brick); both photographs show a coursed brick front with stone only in the dressings: the sills, the keys, the porch and the cornice.

principal_floor_m.note: Read through Chicagology's camera: the principal windows' sills about 2.0 m over grade and the porch's column bases about 0.7 m, the Christmas print's door sill about 1.3 m; the floor is set at 1.0 m between them, the porch's deck on it.

storey_heights_m.note: Read through T-3188's cameras on the pair's front: the upper storey's sills about 5.45-5.66 m and heads 7.4-7.5 m over grade, the principal storey's arches cresting about 4.9 m and the main cornice's soffit about 8.15-8.4 m. The upper floor at 5.15 m stands between the principal arches' crowns and the upper sills; the wall head at 8.3 m is the soffit's line.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rules' brick front. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rules' brick side wall; the north wall is the party wall between the pair. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the one K03 panel k03_brick lays on the side and rear walls; the pictures are monochrome. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

street_front_trim.note: Both photographs show the upper windows' heads laid in the brick (a gauged flat arch under a stone key, the key not built) with no stone lintel; K03's rowlock heads in the front's own brick are the kit's nearest form.

street_front_round_heads.note: Both photographs show the principal storey's street windows round-arched in the brick, a small key at each crown; the arch's head is a carved tympanum over a square sash, built as K06's round fanlight light (its dark glass reads as the tympanum's shadowed carving).

wall_head.note: Both photographs show a deep classical cornice painted light across the pair (its tone the prints' near-white; the paint's hue is reconstructed), a dentil course under a close row of modillions, its soffit about 8.3 m over grade. K01 lays K10's bracketed timber cornice, its brackets made small to stand for the modillions (they stand further apart than the photograph's, and the dentils are not cut).

roof_form.note: Both photographs show a slated mansard over the cornice with pedimented dormers and a railed deck.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the deck behind the railing is not seen from the street; a low hip inside the K05 mansard's upper range. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection, read where its returns show at the pair's corners in both photographs (about 0.6 m).

roof_covering.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the deck's tin and the copper; the lower faces' slate is the photographs' (dark, coursed), its quarry the kit's. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

mansard.note: Chicagology's photograph read through its camera: the straight steep lower faces from the cornice to a curb about 12.0 m over grade (so a 3.7 m rise at about 70 degrees), two pedimented dormers to each house (each pediment's peak triangulated from the two cameras, within 0.3 m: about 2.2 and 7.4 m from 1706's south corner and 3.15 and 8.05 m from 1700's south end, so the pair's dormers are not mirrored, their faces set 0.35 m into the lower face, as far as their pediments clear the curb), their paired sash about 1.45 m square from about 9.2 m (built 1.2 m wide, the kit's widest dormer light), the pediments' peaks about 11.4-11.9 m; the party wall carried up through the roof between the two houses (1706's north wall, which 1700's south hip dies against), and 1700's north end wall carried up past the curb as the Christmas print shows it, coped about 0.6 m over the curb; and an openwork railing about 0.9 m high along the deck's street edge (a white-painted fret in the photograph, laid as K10's cresting pattern in the eave's painted timber: the pattern is the kit's, not the fret's).

stair_tread_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the kit's tread. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The porch's deck runs out about 1.6-2.2 m from the front (the two photographs' cameras triangulated on its corners); the landing is the deck.

stoop_width_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the flight's width; the photographs hide it behind the porch's railings and the trees. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

entrance_bay.note: The door under the porch, read through both cameras.

front_bays.note: Four window columns to each house in both photographs, read through Chicagology's camera at their centres.

street_front_iron.note: Chicagology's photograph shows an iron balconette on a stone shelf before each round-arched principal window outside the porch, about 1.3-1.95 m over grade and a little wider than the light; its diamond panel is not built (the kit's plain bars).

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: no windows on the south wall, the party wall with 1708. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: no windows on the north wall, the party wall with 1700. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: windows in the rear wall beside the wing; no picture shows it. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

sash_by_storey.note: Read through Chicagology's camera: the principal storey's lights about 1.2 m wide (built at the contract's widest, 1.15 m) from about 2.0 m over grade to the arches' crowns about 4.85-4.9 m; the upper storey's about 1.15 m wide from about 5.5 m to 7.45 m.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the sash's kind; the photographs show many-paned upper sashes the kit's two-over-two stands in for. Liberty L-k01-1700-1706-glessner-1871.

rainwater.note: Both photographs show one downpipe down the front at the party line between the two houses; the gutter behind the cornice and the rear pipe are reconstructed.

basement_lights.note: Low basement lights under the principal windows at grade in Chicagology's photograph, behind the area's iron.

chimneys.note: Both photographs show a stack at the party wall over the deck and one toward each house's outer wall; their places on the deck and their heights are reconstructed.

entrance_kit.note: Both photographs show each house's door under a stone porch at its outer end: four Ionic columns along its front (read through both cameras at about 1.15, 2.25, 3.9 and 5.0 m from the outer corner), a plain entablature about 4.0-4.75 m over grade and an iron balcony railing on its deck to about 5.5 m (built 0.6 m high, so its top clears the upper sills). The porch's depth, about 1.9 m, is triangulated on its corners from the two cameras. The flight's place is reconstructed.

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1700-b1) behind the front block: a three-storey range 8.15 m deep and about 4.6 m wide along the pair's south wall, the court between the two houses' ranges open. Its storeys carry the house's floors; its windows and flat roof are reconstructed.

boundary.note: Chicagology's photograph (after 1902) shows the spear-headed iron railing on a low curb running on from before 1708 along 1706's front to a pair of capped piers at the walk to 1706's porch, and stopping there: north of the walk 1706's front, like 1700's, lies open to its lawn behind a low edging stone (T-3212). K11's spear-on-curb railing just inside the street line, 8.7 m before the front: the pair's record puts the public walk 8.9 m out (1708's 9.17 m, the two records 0.3 m apart on one walk), and K11 keeps the curb and piers 0.05 m clear of it, so this line stands about 0.2 m inside 1708's, under a foot, the entrance a pair of walk gates square to the stoop, hung on cast-iron posts with no urn (`posts`, as 1708's): the photograph's gateway posts are dark iron, capped, not stone. The pair is built to its lot's side lines (1706 against 1708, 1700 against the party line), so neither front has a side passage or a side gate (boundary.runs, T-3212). RECONSTRUCTED: the railing's height, the posts' section and height (1708's) and the gates' leaves are the kit's, and the leaves are drawn standing open into the yard, 70 degrees, so the way in reads open from the street, as at 1708 (no picture shows them; liberty L-k14-walks-1700-1706-3212). The 1901 construction photograph (the library's a16-ghm-blog-1700-1706-construction-1901, its camera data/reference_views/<this house>/ghm_construction_1901.json) shows a different, earlier railing on a stone curb running on from 1708's past the party line, with piers before 1706's door and at the party line: that is the railing of 1901, during the build, and is not the one laid here (the match record argues it).

yard.note: T-3212 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). Chicagology's photograph shows 1706's walk coming out from its stoop through the piers to the public walk; the walk is laid in flags from the stoop's foot through the gate. RECONSTRUCTED: the flags, their width and wear, and the bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k14-walks-1700-1706-3212. No turf is laid (lawn 'none'): the yard's grass is the app's own ground, as at 1708. No service walk: the pair has no side passage. No grade_m is set: the app's ground over the pair's base was not measured in this run (1708's beside it rises 7-18 mm, under the flags' 60 mm).
